skill.name: lark-apps
skill.description: Develop, deploy, and administer Lark/Miaoda apps with lark-cli workflows for local development, cloud sessions, publishing, databases, files, environment variables, access scopes, and OpenAPI keys.
skill.summary: Guides Lark/Miaoda app development, deployment, observability, storage, database, environment, access, and API key operations.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, relative documentation links, and Chinese text entropy. Confirmed risks are legitimate secret-handling capabilities: syncing .env.local, displaying environment values, and one-time OpenAPI key output. No prompt injection attempt or encoded payload evidence was found in the inspected skill files.

remediation.issue: Environment workflows can materialize secrets locally or display values.
remediation.suggestion: Keep value redaction as the default, require explicit user intent for include-values, and warn against committing .env.local.

remediation.issue: OpenAPI create and reset return raw keys once.
remediation.suggestion: Preserve one-time display warnings, recommend secret-manager storage, and never log returned keys.

remediation.issue: High-impact database, file, release, access-scope, and environment operations can alter user assets.
remediation.suggestion: Keep dry-run and confirmation gates before online changes, public access changes, deletes, resets, recovery, or publishing.

remediation.issue: Sensitive file override during HTML publish could expose credentials if misused.
remediation.suggestion: Keep blocking .env, .npmrc, and cloud credential files by default, and disclose exact candidates before allow-sensitive.

content.value_statement: Lark app work often spans local code, cloud sessions, databases, files, and releases. This skill routes each task to the right lark-cli workflow with safety checks.
actual_capabilities: Create and update Lark/Miaoda app metadata and resolve app IDs from names or links.
Publish static HTML sites and full-stack releases, then retrieve release or access links.
Guide local full-stack setup, git credential initialization, development, commit, push, and release steps.
Manage app databases, files, environment variables, access scopes, metrics, logs, and traces.
Create, rotate, disable, and scope OpenAPI keys with one-time secret handling rules.
Route cloud Agent sessions and read session status or generated messages.
limitations: Requires lark-cli and a signed-in Lark user with the required scopes.
Does not edit Feishu documents, upload ordinary Drive files, or create native slide decks.
Cannot bypass Lark platform permissions, release failures, storage quotas, or size limits.
High-impact database, environment, publishing, and key actions require clear user authorization.

use_cases.title: Create a Business App
use_cases.description: Plan the app type, create the asset, choose local or cloud development, and prepare the first release.

use_cases.title: Ship Local Full-Stack Changes
use_cases.description: Initialize credentials, work in the app repository, push the correct branch, and publish a verified release.

use_cases.title: Operate a Published App
use_cases.description: Review metrics, logs, database state, file storage, access scope, and environment settings for an existing app.

prompt_templates.title: Create an App
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new app asset.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use lark-apps to create a new full-stack Miaoda app named Approval Tracker. Ask whether I want local development or cloud generation before starting.

prompt_templates.title: Publish Static HTML
prompt_templates.prompt: Use lark-apps to publish the existing ./dist HTML site to a Miaoda app and return the published link after success.

prompt_templates.title: Review App Health
prompt_templates.scenario: Check production behavior for an existing app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use lark-apps to find the app named Order Portal and summarize requests, errors, latency, logs, and traces for the last 24 hours.

prompt_templates.title: Release With Data Checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release workflow with database awareness.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use lark-apps to prepare a full-stack release for app_id app_xxx. Confirm database diffs, push the current branch, create the release, and report the final URL.

output_examples.input: Deploy my local approval app and send me the link.
output_examples.output: The release is finished. The published app URL is ready, and the management link remains available for future changes.

output_examples.input: Show request health for the order app in the last day.
output: Requests and errors were summarized for the selected app.
Latency was reported separately, with slow endpoints called out for follow-up.
Relevant logs and traces were summarized without raw envelope output.

output_examples.output: The exposed key was disabled first. A replacement key was generated once and should be stored in a secret manager.

best_practices: Confirm app ID, environment, and target scope before write, delete, publish, or credential operations.
Use dry-run or preview commands before database migrations, recovery, import, and large static publish operations.
Return summaries, links, and key names; never echo secret values in chat or logs.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a development link or historical published status as proof that the latest version is live.
Do not publish directories that contain real .env, .npmrc, or cloud credential files.
Do not add --yes to destructive database, file, environment, or key actions without user authorization.

faq.question: Does this skill require lark-cli?
faq.answer: Yes. It is built around lark-cli commands and requires an authenticated Lark user session.

faq.question: Can it publish static HTML?
faq.answer: Yes. It can publish an index.html file or a clean static output directory to a Miaoda app.

faq.question: Can it manage production environment variables?
faq.answer: Yes, when the user has permission and explicitly authorizes online environment changes.

faq.question: Will it show secret values?
faq.answer: It should avoid echoing secret values and should use placeholders, files, or secret managers when possible.

faq.question: Can it configure app roles or RBAC?
faq.answer: No. It can set runtime access scope, but app role permissions must be handled in Miaoda web tools.

faq.question: Can it work with existing apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It can resolve app IDs from names, links, or local project metadata before choosing the right workflow.
